packages.heading: Packages
packages.intro: A package is a set of rules content: classes, species, spells, items. The SRD 5.1 comes with the site and is always here. You can add your own packages, homebrew or books you own, from a file: they are checked, kept in this browser only, and never sent anywhere.

load.heading: Add a package
load.hint: Choose the .zip of a package folder, or a .json bundle. You can choose several files at once.

storage.notPersisted: This browser may delete your packages and characters when it runs short of space.

storage.safari: Safari deletes the data of sites you have not opened for a few weeks. Keep the files of your packages; exporting characters to a file comes with a next version.

characters.heading: Characters
characters.intro: Create a character with guidance: every step explains what it changes, and an idea to start from fills in the rest. Or open one of the demo characters to see how a sheet explains every number.

resume.heading: You have a character in progress
resume.text: Pick up where you left off, or start again from the beginning.

content.purpose: Choose the books your character is built from.
content.consequence: Only what these packages contain appears in the next steps; the SRD always comes with the site.
content.recommendation: If this is your first character, the SRD alone is plenty.

concept.purpose: Pick an idea to start from, or skip and choose everything yourself.
concept.consequence: An idea fills in species, class, background and ability scores for you; you can change any of it later.
concept.recommendation: Pick the one that sounds most fun to play: there is no wrong answer.
concept.skipText: No idea to start from: every step starts empty.

species.purpose: Your species is where your character comes from: their body, their senses, a few gifts.
species.consequence: It raises some ability scores and gives traits such as darkvision or resistances.
species.recommendation: Choose the one you like to imagine; the recommended one suits your class best.

class.purpose: Your class is the biggest decision: it sets what you can do in a fight and what you are good at.
class.consequence: It gives your hit points, your proficiencies and the features you gain as you level up.
class.recommendation: A class's primary abilities are the scores it needs most.

background.purpose: Your background is what your character did before becoming an adventurer.
background.consequence: It adds skills, languages or tools, some equipment and a feature.
background.recommendation: Pick the story you like: it matters less than species and class.

abilities.purpose: Your ability scores say how strong, quick, tough, clever, wise and charming your character is.
abilities.consequence: Every roll you make adds the modifier of one of these scores: the higher the score, the better you are at it.
abilities.recommendation: Put your best scores in your class's primary abilities (★); the numbers are already placed that way.

hints.standard-array: Six fixed numbers to share among the abilities: pick where each one goes.
hints.point-buy: Every score starts at 8 and costs points to raise; spend them as you like.
hints.roll: Roll 4d6 six times, drop the lowest die each time, and type the six totals.

abilities.typeRolls: Type all six rolls to place them.

adjustments.title: Manual adjustments
adjustments.note: A number of your own, added to the score's total and shown in its explanation: for a magic item, a house rule or a table decision.

choices.purpose: Some features let you pick: a language, a tool, a skill, your first spells.
choices.consequence: What you pick here goes on your sheet: skills and tools you are good at, languages you speak, spells you can cast.
choices.recommendation: When unsure, pick what fits the character you imagine; nothing here is a wrong answer.
choices.limit: You have chosen them all: remove one to choose another.
choices.none: Nothing else to choose: your choices are complete.

kinds.language: Languages you speak, read and write; the common ones first, the exotic ones for creatures of other planes.
kinds.tool: A tool you know how to use, adding your proficiency bonus when you use it.
kinds.skill: A skill you are trained in: you add your proficiency bonus to its checks.
kinds.expertise: Two skills you are especially good at: your proficiency bonus counts twice for them.
kinds.cantrip: Cantrips are small spells you can cast as often as you like.
kinds.spell: Spells cost a spell slot; you get your slots back after a long rest.
kinds.option: A way your feature works for you; each option says what it does.
kinds.subclass: The path your class takes: it adds features now and at later levels.
kinds.ability: An ability score this feature raises.
kinds.other: A choice this feature asks you to make.
kinds.feat: A special talent that gives your character an extra ability; each one says what it does.

choices.noOptions: The packages you chose offer nothing for this choice: ask your game master, or load the package it comes from.

equipment.purpose: What you carry when the adventure starts: armor, weapons, the tools of your trade, a pack of useful things.
equipment.consequence: Armor and a shield set your Armor Class, weapons your attacks; the rest is there when a situation calls for it.
equipment.recommendation: The first options are a sound start; take coins instead of an item only if you know what you want to buy.

coins.title: Coins
coins.why: The coins your background gives, plus what the items you removed are worth, minus what you bought.

personality.purpose: Who your character is: a name, how they see right and wrong, and what drives them.
personality.consequence: None of this changes a number on the sheet; it is what you play at the table, and what the Game Master can build a story on.
personality.recommendation: A name is all you need to save. For the rest, pick one or two suggestions from your background and make them your own.
personality.name: Name
personality.nameHint: Any name you like; you can change it later from the sheet.
personality.alignmentHint: Your character's moral outlook, from lawful good to chaotic evil; neutral is fine if you are unsure.

hints.traits: Two small things that make your character stand out: a habit, a way of speaking, a passion.
hints.ideals: What your character believes in most, the principle they would not give up.
hints.bonds: A person, a place or a cause your character cares about above everything else.
hints.flaws: A weakness or a vice that others could use against your character.

review.purpose: Your character as the sheet shows it. Check it, then save it in this browser.
review.consequence: Anything still open is listed first, with the step that fixes it; you can save anyway and finish later from the sheet.
review.recommendation: Tap any number on the sheet to see where it comes from.
review.open: One thing is still open | {n} things are still open
review.openHint: None of these stops you from saving, except the name.
